questions.text: In PostgreSQL's general architecture, how does a client application normally interact with the server?

answers.text: Through a driver that implements the PostgreSQL protocol
Only by directly reading cluster files
Only through the server's shared memory segment
Through the system catalog without a network protocol

questions.explanation: The client and server must use the same communication protocol. Normally the client works through a driver that implements the PostgreSQL protocol; a driver may use libpq or implement the protocol itself.

questions.text: Which actions are part of the basic interaction between a PostgreSQL client and server? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Connecting to one of the databases in the cluster
Authenticating the connecting client
Sending SQL queries to the server and receiving results
Directly modifying data pages on disk from the client

questions.explanation: The protocol allows a client to connect to a database in the cluster; the server authenticates the client, then accepts SQL queries, executes them, and returns results. The client does not modify data files directly.

questions.text: Which properties are included in ACID? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Atomicity
Consistency
Isolation
Durability
Automatic backup

questions.explanation: ACID stands for atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability. Backup itself is not one of the ACID properties.

questions.text: What does transaction atomicity mean?

answers.text: A transaction is performed completely or not at all
All transactions must execute sequentially
The transaction result is stored only in memory
A transaction cannot contain more than one SQL command

questions.explanation: Atomicity means 'all or nothing': a transaction's changes are either committed as a whole or not committed.

questions.text: Which statements about ending a transaction are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: BEGIN marks the start of a transaction
COMMIT makes changes permanent
ROLLBACK cancels transaction changes
COMMIT starts a new transaction and cancels the previous one

questions.explanation: In the material, BEGIN marks the start of a transaction, COMMIT makes changes permanent, and ROLLBACK cancels them.

questions.text: Who normally controls transaction boundaries in PostgreSQL?

answers.text: The client application
The operating system
The query planner
The buffer cache

questions.explanation: As a rule, the client application determines which commands belong to a transaction and performs commit or rollback. On the server side, transactions can also be controlled by stored procedures.

questions.text: Which main stages does an ordinary PostgreSQL query pass through? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Parsing
Rewriting
Planning
Execution
Mandatory compilation of the PostgreSQL server

questions.explanation: The material identifies parsing, rewriting, planning, and execution as query-processing stages.

questions.text: Why is the system catalog needed during semantic analysis of a query?

answers.text: To obtain metadata about database objects
To store the result rows of every SELECT
To replace WAL
To manage the client's TCP connection

questions.explanation: The system catalog contains database metadata needed, for example, to determine whether tables and other objects referenced by a query exist.

questions.text: What task does the query planner perform?

answers.text: It chooses an execution plan, including whether to use indexes
It checks the client's password during connection
It creates table files at the operating-system level
It commits every transaction on behalf of the client

questions.explanation: SQL is a declarative language: a query describes the required data, while the planner determines how to obtain it, for example whether an index should be used.

questions.text: Which information helps the planner choose a good plan? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Table sizes
Data distribution in tables
Statistics
The current user's password

questions.explanation: Planning needs statistics containing information about table sizes and data distribution. A user's password is not relevant to plan selection.

questions.text: What does preparing a statement in the extended query protocol provide? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Parsing and rewriting can be done in advance
The parse tree can be stored
Actual parameter values are bound during execution
Every execution must repeat syntactic parsing

questions.explanation: A prepared statement allows parsing and rewriting to be performed in advance and the parse tree to be stored; actual parameter values are bound at execution time.

questions.text: At which stage of a prepared parameterized query are actual parameter values supplied?

answers.text: At the bind stage
At the authentication stage
When postmaster starts
When a page is written to WAL

questions.explanation: After a statement is prepared, actual parameter values are supplied during the bind stage.

questions.text: Which statements about PostgreSQL prepared statements are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: PostgreSQL can sometimes retain a plan and avoid replanning
Using them prevents SQL-code injection
They require a separate backend for each execution of the same query
They always bypass the planner regardless of the situation

questions.explanation: The material notes that a plan can sometimes be reused and that prepared statements help protect against SQL injection. Replanning is not unconditionally excluded.

questions.text: What are cursors used for in the extended query protocol?

answers.text: To fetch a result in parts as needed
To change the data-page size
To restart a backend after an error
To store server parameters instead of postgresql.conf

questions.explanation: A cursor allows a result set to be processed iteratively instead of retrieving the entire result at once.

questions.text: Which statements about a cursor are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: An open cursor is represented by a portal on the server
A cursor can process a result row by row
The cursor's query is implicitly prepared
A cursor must return the entire result to the client in one message

questions.explanation: A cursor allows iterative retrieval of data; an open cursor is represented by a portal, and the query used by it is implicitly prepared.

questions.text: What is the role of the postmaster process in PostgreSQL architecture?

answers.text: It starts the other processes, monitors them, and accepts new connections
It is the local cache of every client process
It performs only SQL query planning
It replaces the connection-pool manager

questions.explanation: When the server starts, postmaster is launched: it creates the other processes, monitors them, and listens for incoming connections.

questions.text: What is stored or allocated in the local memory of a backend process? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Parsed queries and their plans
State of open cursors
System-catalog cache
Space for sorts and joins
The shared buffer cache available to all backends

questions.explanation: Backend local memory is used for the state of a specific serviced connection and for executing its queries. The shared buffer cache is located in shared memory.

questions.text: What happens when a new client connects in PostgreSQL's classic process model?

answers.text: Postmaster creates a separate backend and the client communicates with it thereafter
All clients are always served by one single backend
The client receives direct access to server shared memory
A separate PostgreSQL cluster is created

questions.explanation: For each new client, postmaster starts a backend process; that process also performs authentication.

questions.text: Which mechanisms are used when many processes operate concurrently? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Short-lived locks for shared-memory objects
MVCC and data snapshots for table data
Locking only conflicting changes to data that has not yet been committed
A global halt of all reads until any transaction finishes

questions.explanation: Short-lived locks are used for shared memory. For table data, PostgreSQL relies on MVCC and snapshots, trying to lock only conflicting changes.

questions.text: Which transaction properties are primarily provided by multiversioning?

answers.text: Atomicity, consistency, and isolation
Only durability
Only consistency and durability
Only atomicity

questions.explanation: The material names multiversion concurrency control as the main mechanism supporting the first three transaction properties: atomicity, consistency, and isolation.

questions.text: When does it make sense to use a connection pool?

answers.text: When there are too many clients or connections are opened and closed too frequently
Only when the server has no WAL
Only to change the data-page size
Only to run VACUUM

questions.explanation: A connection pool should be considered when there are many clients or connections are frequently opened and closed.

questions.text: How does a connection pool manager work? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Clients connect to the pool manager instead of directly to PostgreSQL
The manager keeps several server connections open
A free server connection is used for a client's request
Every request must create a new backend and immediately destroy it

questions.explanation: The pool manager accepts client connections and reuses a limited set of open PostgreSQL connections.

questions.text: What should be considered when using a connection pool? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Different clients may use the same backend in turn
Backend local memory can retain state such as prepared queries
From the server's perspective, the number of connections can be kept relatively constant
Pooling makes backend local memory shared among all PostgreSQL processes

questions.explanation: With pooling, multiple clients may share one backend over time, while the backend retains local state. This state must therefore be considered when designing applications.

questions.text: What is the normal PostgreSQL data-page size?

answers.text: 8 KB
512 bytes
64 KB
1 MB

questions.explanation: Files are logically divided into pages (blocks); the normal page size is 8 KB. A different size can be selected only when building the server.

questions.text: Which statements about PostgreSQL storage pages are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A page contains a header and useful data
Free space can remain between them
A running cluster uses one page size
Each page size is selected dynamically for every SELECT

questions.explanation: A page has an internal layout, contains a header and data, and may contain free space when not full. The page size is fixed for the built server, not selected per query.

questions.text: Where is PostgreSQL's buffer cache located?

answers.text: In shared memory accessible to PostgreSQL processes
Only in the local memory of one backend
Only in Cargo.lock
Only on the client side

questions.explanation: PostgreSQL's buffer cache is in shared memory so that different server processes can use cached pages.

questions.text: Which statements about caching and disk I/O are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: PostgreSQL accesses disks through the operating system
The operating system has its own data cache
If a page is not in PostgreSQL's buffer cache, it may still be in the OS cache
A modified page must be synchronously written to disk immediately after every change

questions.explanation: In addition to PostgreSQL's shared buffer cache, there is an operating-system cache. Modified pages may be written to disk later, so durability requires an additional mechanism.

questions.text: Why does PostgreSQL continuously maintain WAL in the context of durability?

answers.text: To replay lost operations after a failure and restore a consistent state
To replace the system catalog
To store all client passwords
To choose a page size for every query

questions.explanation: After a failure, the contents of RAM can be lost together with pages that have not yet been written to disk. The journal allows lost changes to be recovered and data to be returned to a consistent state.

questions.text: Which capabilities can PostgreSQL extensions add? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: New data types and operators
New index types
Background worker processes
Access to external data sources
Mandatory replacement of PostgreSQL's process model with a single thread

questions.explanation: PostgreSQL's architecture supports extensions that add types and operators, index access methods, background tasks, access to external sources, and other capabilities.

questions.text: How are most PostgreSQL extensions typically installed?

answers.text: Most extensions can be installed online without restarting the server
Every extension requires rebuilding the PostgreSQL core
Extensions are available only to client applications
The cluster must be deleted before installing any extension

questions.explanation: The notes emphasize PostgreSQL's extensibility and point out that most extensions can be installed without restarting the server.
